messages:
noah (Support): Multiple customers in ap-southeast-1 reporting severe tail latency on the hosted text-gen API starting ~2026-04-05T10:10Z. p99s hitting 3-6s for tiny prompts. Some requests are timing out. Raising priority.

maya (SRE): which pool/instance group? any config changes in last 48h?

diego (ML Infra): pool name is a100-ap-sg-1. I'm seeing p95 120ms -> 700ms, p99 450ms -> 3.4s. No obvious 5xx spike.

zara (Runtime): grabbing runtime logs. No recent runtime deploys. We do have heavier checkpoint writes overnight for warmup jobs.

noah (Support): tickets: cust-x, cust-y. One enterprise reported a timed-out batch job and opened a billing dispute. Need quick mitigation and clear comms.

maya (SRE): infra-bot, list recent infra events for a100-ap-sg-1.

infra-bot: Recent infra events for a100-ap-sg-1:
- 2026-04-05T09:58Z: Host kernel upgrade 5.15.0-60 applied to 12/48 nodes
- 2026-04-05T10:02Z: NVIDIA driver bump 525.102 -> 535.20 on 14/48 nodes (image bake)
- 2026-04-05T10:05Z: NVMe firmware update to FW_VERSION=XJ34 on 10/48 nodes

diego (ML Infra): driver + nvme fw + kernel bump all within a ~10m window. that's suspicious.

zara (Runtime): pulled dmesg from an affected node, lots of PCIe and GPU errors around 10:11. snippet:

```
Apr  5 10:11:09 host kernel: pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0010
Apr  5 10:11:09 host kernel: NVRM: Xid (0000:65:00): 79, pid=78921, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Apr  5 10:11:10 host kernel: nvme0: I/O 3 QID 1 timeout, aborting
Apr  5 10:11:10 host kernel: nvme0: I/O 3 QID 1 reset controller
```

maya (SRE): nvme resets + gpu fallen off bus = bad latency combo. Could be NVMe controller firmware interacting poorly with new driver or kernel PCIe changes.

diego (ML Infra): checking NVMe perf metrics. Iostat shows avg await jumping to 250-600ms and device util 99% in spikes. That lines up with request tails.

noah (Support): customers want root cause and ETA. Any quick workaround to reduce customer impact?

maya (SRE): immediate actions we can take now:
- cordon/drain the 14 nodes with driver 535.20 and move traffic to nodes still on 525.102
- throttle KV/checkpoint writes (reduce write burst) on the pool
- switch NVMe scheduler to mq-deadline and increase queue_depth on suspect hosts as a temporary tuning
- offer enterprise customers migration to dedicated reserved pool until we stabilize

diego (ML Infra): I'll roll a 2-node canary rollback to driver 525.102 and apply mq-deadline + queue_depth=512, run fio before/after.

infra-bot: fio pre-change on canary:
```
fio --name=randrw --rw=randrw --rwmixread=70 --bs=64k --iodepth=64 --numjobs=4 --size=2G --runtime=60
read: IOPS=18k, BW=110MiB/s, lat (usec): min=80, med=200, max=450000
```

diego (ML Infra): applied scheduler + queue_depth change on canary. re-run fio.

infra-bot: fio post-change on canary:
```
read: IOPS=28k, BW=170MiB/s, lat (usec): min=60, med=120, max=12000
```

zara (Runtime): rolled back driver on canary nodes and restarted runtime. Running quick synthetic request tests.

infra-bot: synthetic request perf on canary after rollback+tuning: p95 120ms, p99 210ms (baseline restored).

noah (Support): reached out to cust-x, offered migration to dedicated pool; they agreed and see latency back to normal after migration.

maya (SRE): plan: phased rollback of driver on remaining affected nodes in low-traffic window + apply nvme tuning cluster-wide. Also will throttle checkpointing for 6h to reduce background write load.

diego (ML Infra): follow-ups: check NVMe SMART and async event logs across fleet for FW XJ34. vendor bulletin suggests FW XJ34 has a corner-case where high concurrent qdepth + mixed rw can trigger internal controller stall. coordinating with vendor/hardware team.

zara (Runtime): short-term runtime guard I can push today: detect repeated NVRM Xid 79/13 and fail fast with a single retry to avoid 10s+ stalls for user requests. I'll ship behind feature flag.

maya (SRE): created incident tracking INF-4237: includes rollback schedule, canary results, and customer comms (owner: maya).

infra-bot: Incident timeline snapshot:
- 2026-04-05T09:58Z: host kernel upgrade rolled to subset of nodes
- 2026-04-05T10:02Z: driver 535.20 rollout began to subset of nodes
- 2026-04-05T10:05Z: NVMe firmware XJ34 applied to subset of nodes
- 2026-04-05T10:11Z: first customer latency alerts and device errors observed
- 2026-04-05T10:32Z: canary rollback + NVMe tuning -> canary p99 restored

noah (Support): we have a billing dispute from cust-y; I'll flag to billing and record mitigation steps so we can expedite.

diego (ML Infra): action items:
- audit NVMe async event counts and SMART across fleet for FW XJ34 (owner: diego)
- coordinate vendor firmware fix or re-flash plan if needed (owner: diego + hw)
- add fio+gpu stress preflight to image bake to catch these combos (owner: infra eng)

zara (Runtime): action items:
- runtime fast-fail + retry on GPU-reset detection (owner: zara)
- add per-request telemetry to better correlate nvme latency windows with token emission stalls (owner: zara)

maya (SRE): action items:
- schedule full rollback of driver to 525.102 during maintenance window with monitoring (owner: maya)
- produce postmortem and customer-facing incident note (owner: maya)

noah (Support): I'll update all open tickets and send an enterprise incident summary to affected customers. Marking thread resolved for now; will re-open if regressions come back. :white_check_mark:
